standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 3 — kitchen helper safety and no-heat preparation
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice the kitchen reset. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult writes a short list of three or four items needed for a planned task and the learner runs the kitchen reset at their own kitchen counter or table: returning clutter to its own spot, wiping the cleared surface with a cloth, laying out exactly the listed items, and finishing with a look-only scan where the learner looks at, without touching, the stove knobs and nearby appliances before calling the reset finished.
safetyNotes: The safety scan is look-only. The learner never touches a stove knob, appliance switch, or knife during this lesson, even just to check whether it is off.
If anything looks like it might still be on, or the learner is not sure, the correct move is to stop and ask a trusted adult to check — that asking counts as success.
materials: learner-local: a short written list of three or four items for a planned task

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe one specific thing you looked at during your safety scan, like a stove knob or an appliance, and explain why looking at it, without touching it, before starting matters.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Reset sequence: Completes all four reset steps in order. | Safety scan accuracy: Names at least one specific stove knob or appliance looked at, without touching it, during the safety scan. | List discipline: Sets out exactly the items on the list, nothing more or less. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner run the kitchen reset on a different household surface, like a craft table before a project, adapting the same four steps (clear, wipe, gather exact items, a look-only safety scan) to a space where the thing to look at, never touch, might be an outlet or a pair of scissors instead of a stove.

resources.title: the kitchen reset coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult writes a short list of three or four items needed for a planned task and the learner runs the kitchen reset at their own kitchen counter or table: returning clutter to its own spot, wiping the cleared surface with a cloth, laying out exactly the listed items, and finishing with a look-only scan where the learner looks at, without touching, the stove knobs and nearby appliances before calling the reset finished.
Coach direction: Look at your kitchen counter or table before you touch anything.
Learner prompt: Name two things sitting on the counter right now that do not belong there for this task.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: the kitchen reset complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Run the four-step kitchen reset in order: clear the surface, wipe it with a cloth, set out only the items on your list, and finish with a look-only safety scan: look at, but do not touch, the stove knobs and nearby appliances.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I moved every item that didn't belong on the counter back to its own spot.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wiped the cleared surface with a clean cloth until it looked and felt clean.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I set out only the exact items on my list, nothing extra.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I looked at (without touching) the stove knobs and any nearby small appliance, and each one appeared off or unplugged, before I finished.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: the kitchen reset minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe one specific thing you looked at during your safety scan, like a stove knob or an appliance, and explain why looking at it, without touching it, before starting matters.

Success checks: Reset sequence: Completes all four reset steps in order. | Safety scan accuracy: Names at least one specific stove knob or appliance looked at, without touching it, during the safety scan. | List discipline: Sets out exactly the items on the list, nothing more or less.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: the kitchen reset supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional the kitchen reset condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Reset sequence: Completes all four reset steps in order. | Safety scan accuracy: Names at least one specific stove knob or appliance looked at, without touching it, during the safety scan. | List discipline: Sets out exactly the items on the list, nothing more or less..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
